• Three years on from the onset of the pandemic, concerns regarding the academic
impact of the pandemic on students.
• Thus far, Indiana state assessment data (ILEARN and WIDA-ACCESS) indicate large to
severe academic impacts and little recovery (stabilization) through 2022.
• The release of NAEP data in 2022 (with pre-pandemic comparisons to 2019) has only
amplified concerns about the impact of the pandemic on students.

Pandemic Related Academic Recovery in Indiana 2

Academic Impact & Recovery
• The pandemic and all the ensuing disruptions functioned/
functions as an “academic headwind”, impeding (in general) the
academic progress of students.
• This is Academic Impact and shows up in educational
assessments as:
▪ Decrease in student growth (i.e. decrease in velocity = deceleration).
▪ Decrease in student attainment.
• Academic Recovery would show up in education assessments
as an increase in student growth (i.e., increase in velocity =
acceleration) leading to an increase in student attainment.
Pandemic Related Academic Recovery in Indiana 3

Assessment Data
• As in 2021 and 2022, to investigate academic recovery in 2023 we
utilized two primary sources of data
• ILEARN state summative assessment data
• WIDA-ACCESS state English Language Proficiency Data
• For attainment comparisons, 2023 data is compared to 2019 data.
• For growth comparisons, current growth data (2022 to 2023) is
compared to pre-pandemic growth data (2018 to 2019).

Pandemic Related Academic Recovery in Indiana 4

Last Year I Mentioned Cautions Going Forward
• Maintaining scales to pre-pandemic years will increasingly become
challenging for states.
• Two views of returning to “normal”
• Is the education system returning to normal?
• Are students impacted by the pandemic returning to normal?
• The education system returning to normal means the education system
supports rates of student learning consistent with what was observed pre-
pandemic.
• The education system can return to “normal” without student returning to
normal.
• To catch-up to where they would have been academically, students must
learn at rates exceeding what was observed pre-pandemic.

Pandemic Related Academic Recovery in Indiana 9

Big Picture
• As we found last year, the Indiana’s education system has, on
average, “recovered” to support rates of learning that it did pre-
pandemic. To avoid confusion with “student recovery”, we called
this “stabilization”
• In 2023, the system followed trend with 2022 and demonstrated, on
average, rates of growth consistent with what was observed pre-
pandemic.
• Given the academic losses incurred by students from 2019 to 2021,
typical progress is not, in general, sufficient for student recovery.
• Thus, individual students continue to fall below 2019 attainment
levels.

Pandemic Related Academic Recovery in Indiana 19

Summary
• There is a modest improvement in results, overall, from 2021-2022
and 2022-2023
• However, rates of growth for most students are insufficient to catch
them up to where they would have been had the pandemic not
occurred.
• In most grades and content areas lower achieving students are
demonstrating rates of learning below what was seen pre-pandemic
whereas their high achieving counterparts are demonstration rates
of learning above what was seen pre-pandemic.
• This suggest a K-shaped recovery where, on average, low achieving
students don’t recover and their higher achieving counterparts do.
